root_cause.text: In the SMB server RDMA transport (`fs/smb/server/transport_rdma.c`), `smb_direct_post_send_data()` freed the same `sendmsg` object twice because `smb_direct_flush_send_list()` already frees moved send messages via `smb_direct_free_sendmsg()`, but the caller still jumped to `err:` and called `smb_direct_free_sendmsg(sc, msg)` again after a flush failure/path.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds the comment “From here msg is moved to send_ctx and we should not free it explicitly,” changes the flush error path from `goto err;` to `goto flush_failed;`, and the commit message explicitly states “smb_direct_flush_send_list() already calls smb_direct_free_sendmsg(), so we should not call it again after post_sendmsg() moved it to the batch list.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the send-data cleanup path so transferred send messages are not freed twice when flush of the send list fails.
intent_record.what: The function `smb_direct_post_send_data()` was updated by inserting a comment stating that `msg` is moved to `send_ctx` and should not be freed explicitly from that point onward. Also, the error path after `smb_direct_flush_send_list()` was changed from `goto err;` to `goto flush_failed;`, and a new `flush_failed:` label was added before `header_failed:` so that the flush-failure path skips `smb_direct_free_sendmsg(sc, msg)`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents double-free or invalid free of `msg` after ownership has been transferred into `send_ctx`. If flushing the send list fails, the code now bypasses the explicit send-message free and proceeds directly to the shared cleanup that restores credits, preserving the correct ownership/lifecycle semantics.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly matches the reported root cause: it fixes the SMB RDMA send-data cleanup path to avoid double-freeing a sendmsg object after flush failure, which is exactly the vulnerability condition.

candidates.rationale: This jump sends execution to the error path after a flush failure, where the caller then frees msg again even though smb_direct_flush_send_list() may already have freed transferred send messages, leading to a double free.
This cleanup call on the shared error path is the second free of msg after the flush path has already freed it, which directly embodies the double-free root cause.

vuln_statements.explanation: This cleanup statement is reached after the send-list flush failure path, where transferred send messages may already have been freed by smb_direct_flush_send_list(), so calling smb_direct_free_sendmsg(sc, msg) again causes the double free.
This jump routes execution to the shared error cleanup path that unconditionally frees msg again, which is the control-flow step that makes the double-free possible after a flush failure.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function body includes the new batch-credit handling and the extra flush path, but it does not show the double-free bug described in the root cause. In particular, `smb_direct_post_send_data()` now allocates a temporary batch context (`if (!send_ctx) { ... }`), acquires a send batch credit via `wait_for_send_bcredit(sc, send_ctx);`, and after `post_sendmsg(sc, send_ctx, msg)` it conditionally flushes only when using the temporary context: `if (send_ctx == &_send_ctx) { ret = smb_direct_flush_send_list(sc, send_ctx, true); if (ret) goto err; }`. The error path still calls `smb_direct_free_sendmsg(sc, msg);`, but the commit adds corresponding credit-release logic in `smb_direct_flush_send_list()` and in the `lcredit_failed:` path (`atomic_add(send_ctx->credit, &sc->send_io.bcredits.count); send_ctx->credit = 0;`), which indicates the fix is present here to prevent the prior stream corruption / premature empty-send issue. The specific double-free construct from the root cause is not visible in this revised code.
